description: Head-to-head falsification summary: four discriminating observables comparing KBC void/MOND model vs TEP isochrony violation. Observable 1 and the overlapping redshift-profile observables 3 and 4 are direct comparisons. Observable 2 quantifies how the indicator divergence propagates into the peculiar velocity field.

observables.tep_prediction: DMceph < DMtrgb (Cepheid distances compressed by acoustic clock bias)
observables.tep_result: CF4: Δμ = -0.0799 ± 0.0242 mag (3.30σ; 2.55σ with 0.02 mag ZP covariance), N=22, 17/22 Cepheid shorter; JWST filter-corrected (Step 50): Δμ = -0.0420 ± 0.0237 mag (1.77σ; -0.0600 ± 0.0262 mag, 2.29σ excl. M101); Same-team MF2023 VIH × JWST TRGB (Step 50, N=13): Δμ = -0.196 ± 0.016 mag (13/13 negative, 3.67σ binomial); Same-team MF2023 band differential (Step 49, N=20): -2.01e6 mag (3.68σ); LMC internal spatial gradient (Step 60, N=2,116): r = -0.072 (3.30σ, zero anchor ZP).

observables.tep_prediction: Cepheid H0 inflates bulk flow; Δv = -3.2·d km/s from indicator divergence (Observable 1)
observables.void_prediction: No calibration dependence (bulk flow is gravitational)
observables.tep_result: Mean BF reduction: 1.9%, RMS shift: 839 km/s, 89% of galaxies |shift|>200 km/s (N=38053)
observables.note: This is a quantification of how the indicator divergence (Observable 1) propagates into the peculiar velocity field, not an independent falsification test.

observables.tep_prediction: Flat H0(z) ≈ 73 for global M_B (zero-point inheritance)
observables.tep_result: χ²_red(TEP) = 2.31 (n_fit=0.00), χ²_red(Const) = 1.98, ΔAIC(Void−TEP) = 0.1, best=const; Fixed predictions: ΔAIC(Gaussian−flat) = 20.2, ΔAIC(Exponential−flat) = 79.3; flexible profiles: ΔAIC(Void−TEP) = 0.1
observables.significance: Fixed predictions: ΔAIC(Gaussian−flat) = 20.2, ΔAIC(Exponential−flat) = 79.3; flexible profiles: ΔAIC(Void−TEP) = 0.1
observables.comparison_scope: fixed published void predictions versus flat global-M_B prediction

fixed_prediction_comparison.tep_n03_reference_note: n=0.3 applied to SN data is NOT the global M_B prediction
fixed_prediction_comparison.note: Void curves calibrated to HBK20/Mazurenko et al. 2025 published convergence (1σ Planck at z≈1.8)

observables.tep_prediction: Flat H0(z) for global M_B (zero-point inheritance)
observables.note: The absolute H0 at z > 0.25 is NOT independent — Pantheon+ uses MU_SH0ES with M_B=-19.253 from Cepheid anchors. The meaningful test is the relative evolution (common zero-point cancels). The host-mass dependence of the TEP effect is established in TEP-H0 (Paper 11).

overall_assessment.verdict: TEP strongly favored — all direct falsification tests (3/3) support TEP over the KBC void model. The indicator-specific distance divergence (3.30σ (CF4), 3.68σ (MF2023 band), 3.67σ (MF2023×JWST 13/13), 3.30σ (LMC internal)) is dataset/reduction dependent. The H0(z) redshift profile (Fixed predictions: ΔAIC(Gaussian−flat) = 20.2, ΔAIC(Exponential−flat) = 79.3; flexible profiles: ΔAIC(Void−TEP) = 0.1) and the calibration-independent relative evolution (ΔH0(low→high) = +1.2 km/s/Mpc (no decline), ΔAIC(Void_Gauss−TEP)=11.7, ΔAIC(Void_Exp−TEP)=40.0) — two views of the same Pantheon+ redshift-profile test — provide the decisive falsification of the void model.

tep_prediction: Redshift-profile test (Sections 7/8) should favor TEP; indicator divergence (Section 5) is dataset/reduction dependent
void_prediction: The KBC void/MOND model predicts indicator-independent distances, calibration-independent bulk flow, and a gradual H0(z) decline. Falsification occurs if the direct tests favor TEP.
methodology: Four discriminating observables compiled from upstream step results (steps 30, 31, 32, 34, 40). Each observable carries TEP and void predictions, measured results, and significance. Direct falsification tests (observables 1, 3, 4) are weighted most heavily in the overall verdict. Observable 2 is a quantification of the indicator divergence propagation, not an independent test.

provenance.pipeline_block: Block III — TEP reconstruction and synthesis

scientific_context: Head-to-head falsification of the KBC void/MOND model against the TEP isochrony-violation framework. The four observables span indicator-specific distance divergence, bulk-flow calibration sensitivity, the H0(z) redshift profile, and calibration-independent relative evolution. The combined verdict determines whether the void model is falsified.
